result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers find the same problems with sound reasoning and give the same core fixes: 1rem body text, a roomy line height, #222 text, a ~65ch line cap, left-aligned text and 1em paragraph spacing. B edges ahead because its replacement CSS is a complete, self-contained layout (centred, padded, with explicit text-align: left). It also warns that newsletter email clients often ignore max-width and rem. A's choice to cap only the text elements is thoughtful, but its CSS covers only p, ul, ol and h2, and it doesn't address the email case. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers find the same core problems and give runnable fixes: rem-based 16px text, a line height of about 1.5–1.6, #222 for contrast, a 65ch cap, left alignment and 1em paragraph spacing. B is a bit more detailed on the heading and caps the width on the text elements so images and tables can stay wider. A centers the column and adds a useful warning that email clients may ignore max-width and rem. Those strengths balance out.
